title: 硕鼠
author: 佚名（《诗经·魏风》）
authorEn: Anonymous (Book of Songs, Airs of Wei)
intro: Farmers shout at a fat rat that keeps eating their grain — and everyone knew the “rat” was the lord who taxed them. One of the oldest protest songs in the world, ending with the dream of a land where life is fair.
analysis: 这首诗表面上在骂一只大老鼠：别再吃我的黍、我的麦、我的苗了！我养了你三年，你却一点也不照顾我。其实“硕鼠”是在比喻那些只拿不干、用重税剥削农民的统治者。直接说出来太危险，就借一个人人讨厌的动物来骂，这种手法叫“比”，也就是比喻。全诗三章，每章只换几个字（黍—麦—苗，顾—德—劳），越唱越愤怒。最后农民发誓要离开，去寻找一个“乐土”——没有剥削、能过上公平日子的地方。这个“乐土”成了中国人心中理想社会的说法，今天“乐土”这个词还在用。
analysisEn: On the surface this song is yelling at a big rat: stop eating my millet, my wheat, my young crops! I fed you for three years and you never cared about me. But the listeners all understood that the “big rat” stood for the rulers who took the farmers’ harvest in heavy taxes and gave nothing back. Saying that openly was dangerous, so the song hides its target behind an animal everyone hates. This technique is called bǐ (“comparison”) — one of the three classic methods of the Book of Songs. The three verses are almost identical, changing only a few words each time (millet, wheat, young crops), and the anger builds with every repetition. At the end the farmers swear to leave and look for a lètǔ, a “happy land” where people are treated fairly. That word stuck: Chinese still calls a paradise or an ideal place 乐土 today. It is a rare voice from ordinary people nearly 3,000 years ago, and it still sounds fresh.
background: The Book of Songs gathers 305 songs from roughly the 11th to the 6th century BC; most authors are unknown. This one comes from the state of Wei (魏, in today’s southern Shanxi), a small, poor state whose folk songs often complain about greedy rulers.
pronunciation: 女：通“汝”，读 rǔ（“三岁贯女”“逝将去女”），意思是“你”。乐土、乐国、乐郊的“乐”读 lè。爰 yuán。永号：号 háo，大声哭喊，不读 hào。谁：古诗文习惯读 shuí。逝：通“誓”，读 shì。“女”“号”机器朗读易错，已在“朗读用字”列替换同音字。
version: 采用通行《毛诗》文本，全诗三章，每章八句；网站按两个四字句为一行排版。“逝将去女”的“逝”，一说通“誓”（发誓），一说是语气词，教材多取“誓”。

lines.py: shuò shǔ shuò shǔ, wú shí wǒ shǔ
lines.lit: Big rat, big rat, do not eat my millet!
lines.en: Big rat, big rat — keep your teeth off my millet!

lines.py: sān suì guàn rǔ, mò wǒ kěn gù
lines.lit: Three years I have served you, yet you will not look after me.
lines.en: Three years I have fed you, and you never once cared for me.

lines.py: shì jiāng qù rǔ, shì bǐ lè tǔ
lines.lit: I swear I will leave you and go to that happy land.
lines.en: I swear I’ll leave you now for a happier land.

lines.py: lè tǔ lè tǔ, yuán dé wǒ suǒ
lines.lit: Happy land, happy land — there I will find my place.
lines.en: A happy land, a happy land — there I’ll find a place to live.

lines.py: shuò shǔ shuò shǔ, wú shí wǒ mài
lines.lit: Big rat, big rat, do not eat my wheat!
lines.en: Big rat, big rat — keep your teeth off my wheat!

lines.py: sān suì guàn rǔ, mò wǒ kěn dé
lines.lit: Three years I have served you, yet you show me no kindness.
lines.en: Three years I have fed you, and you never showed me any kindness.

lines.py: shì jiāng qù rǔ, shì bǐ lè guó
lines.lit: I swear I will leave you and go to that happy country.
lines.en: I swear I’ll leave you now for a happier country.

lines.py: lè guó lè guó, yuán dé wǒ zhí
lines.lit: Happy country, happy country — there I will get what is fair.
lines.en: A happy country, a happy country — there I’ll be treated fairly.

lines.py: shuò shǔ shuò shǔ, wú shí wǒ miáo
lines.lit: Big rat, big rat, do not eat my young crops!
lines.en: Big rat, big rat — keep your teeth off my young crops!

lines.py: sān suì guàn rǔ, mò wǒ kěn láo
lines.lit: Three years I have served you, yet you never reward my toil.
lines.en: Three years I have fed you, and you never thanked me for my work.

lines.py: shì jiāng qù rǔ, shì bǐ lè jiāo
lines.lit: I swear I will leave you and go to those happy fields.
lines.en: I swear I’ll leave you now for happier fields.

lines.py: lè jiāo lè jiāo, shuí zhī yǒng háo
lines.lit: Happy fields, happy fields — who would cry out there forever?
lines.en: Happy fields, happy fields — who would still be wailing there?

words.note: 硕：大，现代汉语“硕大”“硕果”。
古义，同“毋”，表示禁止；今天说“别”“不要”。
北方的一种粮食，今天叫“黍子”“黄米”。
岁：年。古义，今天“岁”多指年龄。
古义，侍奉、供养；今天“贯”多指穿过、连贯。
通“汝”，第二人称，不是“女人”的“女”。

words.en: you are unwilling to care for me
words.note: 倒装，正常语序是“莫肯顾我”。
通“誓”。现代汉语“逝”指去世、消逝。
古义是“离开”，和今天“去北京”的“去”方向相反。
古义，前往；今天“适合”的“适”是另一个意思。
古义，公道；现代汉语“正直”“理直气壮”还保留。
今天“号啕大哭”“呼号”仍读 háo。

imagery.name: 禾
imagery.zh: 黍、麦、苗是农民一年的辛苦，被老鼠吃掉，就是被重税夺走。
imagery.en: Millet, wheat and young crops are a year of the farmers’ sweat — eaten by the rat, taken by taxes.
